SARAH JENKINS
Email: sarah.jenkins@gmail.com | Phone: 555-019-2834
Location: Seattle, WA | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/sarahjenkins

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Backend Engineer specialized in distributed Java microservices, Apache Kafka event streaming, and high-throughput PostgreSQL architectures.

EDUCATION
University of Washington — B.S. in Computer Science (2020 – 2024)

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java, SQL, Go, TypeScript
Frameworks: Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Hibernate, Express
Developer Tools: Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Terraform, Git, Jenkins
Databases & Queues: PostgreSQL, Apache Kafka, Redis, DynamoDB

PROJECTS
CloudScale E-Commerce Payment Gateway
• Engineered high-throughput distributed transaction pipeline processing 15,000 requests/sec with Spring Boot and Kafka.
• Implemented distributed saga pattern with PostgreSQL optimistic locking preventing double-spend anomalies.
• Reduced p99 checkout latency by 45% using Redis read-through caching.

Distributed Real-Time Telemetry Pipeline
• Architected multi-region AWS Kinesis and Kafka consumer group streaming 50M daily events into Snowflake.
• Integrated automated dead-letter queues (DLQ) achieving 99.99% event delivery reliability.

questions.question: Walk me through your background and the primary technical challenges you focused on in your engineering projects.
questions.why_this_question: Evaluates professional communication, engineering narrative, and technical self-awareness.

questions.question: In CloudScale E-Commerce Payment Gateway, can you walk me through your end-to-end architecture from data ingestion to user consumption?
questions.source_claim: Built using Spring Boot, Kafka, AWS
questions.why_this_question: Validates system design reasoning and architectural ownership in CloudScale E-Commerce Payment Gateway.

questions.question: In CloudScale E-Commerce Payment Gateway, why did you choose Spring Boot over standard alternatives, and what specific latency or throughput trade-offs did you encounter?
questions.source_claim: Engineered high-throughput distributed transaction pipeline processing 15,000 requests/sec with Spring Boot and Kafka.
questions.why_this_question: Probes deep understanding of framework internals, memory usage, and performance constraints.

questions.question: In your Distributed Real-Time Telemetry Pipeline, how did you design the indexing and search algorithms to maintain low query latency under high load?
questions.source_claim: Integrated automated dead-letter queues (DLQ) achieving 99.99% event delivery reliability.
questions.why_this_question: Probes algorithmic depth, vector/database indexing, and scalability in Distributed Real-Time Telemetry Pipeline.

questions.question: How did you implement security and authorization in your Distributed Real-Time Telemetry Pipeline, and how did you prevent race conditions during concurrent user actions?
questions.why_this_question: Evaluates security architecture, token validation, and multi-tenant thread safety.

questions.question: Comparing your database and storage choices across your projects, what empirical criteria determined when to choose relational vs document vs vector stores?
questions.why_this_question: Evaluates senior-level architectural maturity and polyglot data modeling expertise.

questions.question: When streaming telemetry or processing asynchronous event queues, what QoS/backpressure strategy did you use to prevent worker thread pool exhaustion?
questions.why_this_question: Examines mastery of concurrency models, worker pools, and memory leaks.

questions.question: Describe the single hardest bug, race condition, or memory leak you encountered during development, and walk me through your step-by-step root-cause analysis.
questions.why_this_question: Reveals debugging methodology, profiler usage (gdb, memory profilers), and intellectual honesty.

questions.question: If Amazon deployed your primary engineering system across 1,000 distributed edge nodes with a 99.99% availability SLA, what are the first 3 architectural bottlenecks that will break, and how would you redesign the system?
questions.why_this_question: Evaluates readiness for Amazon's enterprise-scale distributed systems and high-availability operations.
